name: Can a pool removal be done while living at the house?

mainEntity.name: Can homeowners stay in the house during in-ground pool removal, and how disruptive is the process?
mainEntity.text: Can homeowners stay in the house during in-ground pool removal, and how disruptive is the process?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most pool removals are done while the family remains in the home, but the project can be disruptive. Expect noise from breaking concrete, truck traffic, dust, temporary fencing, and occasional interruptions to driveway or side-yard access. If the pool sits close to the house, the disruption can be more noticeable. Homeowners should ask the contractor how work hours are handled, how dust is controlled, and which parts of the property will be unavailable during demolition. In Los Angeles neighborhoods with tight lot lines, respectful staging and communication matter a lot. The process is usually manageable if the crew protects the site and keeps the work organized, but it is not a quiet project. Planning ahead helps reduce stress while the job is underway.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, most homeowners can stay in the house during pool removal, but there will be noise, dust, equipment traffic, and temporary access restrictions. The level of disruption depends on yard layout, access routes, and whether demolition happens near living spaces. Good scheduling and site protection reduce the impact.
